# google_scc_v2_organization_source_finding

A Cloud Security Command Center's (Cloud SCC) finding. A finding is 
a record of assessment data like security, risk, health, or privacy, 
that is ingested into Security Command Center for presentation, notification, 
analysis, policy testing, and enforcement. For example, a cross-site scripting (XSS) 
vulnerability in an App Engine application is a finding.


To get more information about OrganizationSourceFinding, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/reference/rest/v2/organizations.sources.locations.findings)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs)

## Example Usage - Scc V2 Organization Source Finding Basic


```hcl
resource "google_scc_v2_organization_source_finding" "custom_source_finding" {
  organization = "123456789"
  source       = "my-source"
  location     = "global"
  finding_id   = "custom-finding-id"
  
  resource_name= "//cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/organizations/123"
  state        = "ACTIVE"
  category     = "MEDIUM_RISK_ONE"
  event_time   = "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `organization` -
  (Required)
  The organization whose Cloud Security Command Center the Source
  lives in.

* `source` -
  (Required)
  The numeric ID of the source for the finding.

* `finding_id` -
  (Required)
  The numeric ID of the source for the finding.

* `resource_name` -
  (Required)
  The full resource name of the Google Cloud resource this finding is for, in the format
  `//cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/organizations/123`


- - -


* `state` -
  (Optional)
  The state of the finding.
  Possible values are: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`.

* `category` -
  (Optional)
  The additional taxonomy group within findings from a given source.
  Example: XSS_FLASH_INJECTION

* `event_time` -
  (Optional)
  The time the finding was first detected. 
  If an existing finding is updated, then this is the time the update occurred.

* `location` -
  (Optional)
  The Security Command Center location in which to create a finding. 
  When data residency controls are enabled, this attribute specifies the location in which the resource is located and applicable.
  If not provided, Use global as default.


## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `organizations/{{organization}}/sources/{{source}}/locations/{{location}}/findings`


## Timeouts

## Import


OrganizationSourceFinding can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `organizations/{{organization}}/sources/{{source}}/locations/{{location}}/findings/{{name}}`
* `{{organization}}/{{source}}/{{location}}/{{name}}`


In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import OrganizationSourceFinding using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "organizations/{{organization}}/sources/{{source}}/locations/{{location}}/findings/{{name}}"
  to = google_scc_v2_organization_source_finding.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), OrganizationSourceFinding can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_scc_v2_organization_source_finding.default organizations/{{organization}}/sources/{{source}}/locations/{{location}}/findings/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_scc_v2_organization_source_finding.default {{organization}}/{{source}}/{{location}}/{{name}}
```
